### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f8126048793e9b5760f87130cb83645f4c185ce` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2657ad59816f2cfe19f5449528335d49f67ee082` — the merge of head `1d178dcfcb54760c22c6c01d99bbdb90bd8965d9` into base `9f8126048793e9b5760f87130cb83645f4c185ce`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2657ad59816f2cfe19f5449528335d49f67ee082 && git checkout 2657ad59816f2cfe19f5449528335d49f67ee082
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9f8126048793e9b5760f87130cb83645f4c185ce 1d178dcfcb54760c22c6c01d99bbdb90bd8965d9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9f8126048793e9b5760f87130cb83645f4c185ce && git merge --no-ff 1d178dcfcb54760c22c6c01d99bbdb90bd8965d9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f8126048793e9b5760f87130cb83645f4c185ce
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## ✅ ACCEPT, with a patch round owed: PR #23620 at `121ac4d711` (#23181 slice 3). It lands once the patch head is green and the changeset question below is settled

## 席位核对

1. **Shape, read on GitHub:**
   - The PR is a draft against `main`, head `121ac4d711`. Line 1 is `Part of #23181`, and the body carries no closing keyword. Line 2 is a bare, line-initial `Clause-②: no`. Assignee `os-bill`.
   - Files: 6, +122 / −3. Five row test files and the new `packages/verify/src/boot-warm-up.testkit.ts`, all inside the claim's surface (at most five row files, plus one shared helper there).
   - `check-governed-merges --pr 23620`: NOT governed. No `content/docs/releases/` change.
2. **The hunks:**
   - Each of the five files adds one module-scope `await warmUpBoot(...)` with the options its own first boot uses.
   - `handle.test.ts` replaces `vi.resetModules()` with a query-suffixed import of `./handle.fixture.js`. That gives a fresh instance of the fixture alone, so the whole graph is no longer re-evaluated.
   - The helper boots its own empty app on its own database, signs in, signs up, and stops before the file's first hook. Nothing a case asserts on is shared.
   - Titles are unchanged (sha256 of the title lines) and the `expect(` counts are unchanged (77, 10, 13, 12, 39). No timeout moved.
3. **Measurement:**
   - All 24 row files were measured isolated, and the whole package before and after.
   - Interleaved A/B, three rounds per changed file. Isolated medians:
     - handle 9524 → 4336 ms;
     - the trigger door 4328 → 1616 ms;
     - the action door 4223 → 1562 ms;
     - served-composition 7308 → 5006 ms;
     - delete-behavior 9889 → 8023 ms.
   - Five ablations went red exactly as predicted, each restore proven by blob.
   - **H2 and H3 are falsified with measurements and accepted as such.** The top three files already share their boots, and no row file had a warm-up.
4. **Gates:**
   - Local: 50 derived, 50 run. Package: 41 files and 362 tests pass; typecheck exit 0.
   - CI on `121ac4d711`, read in this act: 39 check-runs, 24 success, 6 skipped, 6 `in_progress`, 3 failures.
     - **`Check Changeset`:** no label (see 5).
     - **`Lint · repo & tooling gates`, and `Lint & Repo Gates` with it:** a real red, owned by this PR. Its failing step is `@objectstack/verify stand-in erasure guard` (`pnpm check:verify-stand-in`). `scripts/check-verify-stand-in-erasure.mjs` scans every exported function in a non-test `packages/verify/src` file whose first parameter is typed with an interface the package declares and `index.ts` exports as a type. `warmUpBoot(opts: BootOptions = {})` is one: `BootOptions` is declared at `harness.ts:181` and exported at `index.ts:16`. Unclassified, it fails the run by design. The guard's own remedy is a human classification: `NOT_A_STAND_IN` with its reason, or the guarded set. A patch round goes to the same dev.
5. **Changeset:**
   - The seat checked the criterion for itself. `@objectstack/verify` publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. The diff adds only test files and one `*.testkit.ts` that `index.ts` does not export, and the dev measured 0 hits for its names in a rebuilt `dist/`. So the PR is tests-only, and `skip-changeset` is the right form by its criterion.
   - ⚠️ **The label is not applied by this seat.** The dev's own write of it was refused by the session's permission classifier. The seat does not re-issue a write that was refused, so the label goes to the maintainer.
6. **The report's open questions, answered:**
   - **(1) The next slice for the other 19 files:** option A. The next hourly refresh first reads whether the two claimed rows left the list. Then a slice of up to five of the eight files that project under 10 s, re-measured with interleaved A/B.
   - **(2) The top three** (`unique-scope`, `parent-write-reach`, `delete-behavior`): they stay on #23181.
     - Their remedy is a measured source slice of this same card, on the harness boot cost (the card's "what it waits on"), opened with a boot profile.
     - Option B (a declared budget under ruling `6181973363`) is not taken without an explicit reading of that ruling.
     - Option C (a shared scrypt memo) is an add-on once a shared home exists.
   - **(3) The trade:** option A, keep the whole-boot warm-up. It follows the AGENTS.md clocked-window convention, and the extra cost is bounded at about one boot per file.
7. **Deviations:**
   - Accepted: the ablations mutated four source files outside the surface, one run each, each restore proven; one 106 ms probe ran outside the lock; the merge commit carries git's default message.
   - **The PR body sentence the report corrects** ("stayed within ±2 s across the rounds", in "What the move costs") is wrong for two files. The seat writes the dev's replacement into the body when the patch round lands, per the role file: the dev never `PATCH`es the body.
8. **Out of scope:** the three observations are carried by this card, as the answers in 6 say. They are in `Acceptance notes`, and no card is owed.

**Landing:**
- No contract review is owed: test files only, `Clause-②: no`, not governed.
- Once the patch head is true-green, `skip-changeset` is on, and the body correction is written, the seat flips the PR ready and arms auto-merge.
- At the merge, #23181 goes back to `pm:queue`, unassigned, with a `Release:` line naming the remaining rows.
